required_audit_coverage.name: required_audit_coverage
required_audit_coverage.detail: report covers all 45 Required Audit items with substantive aligned answers
required_audit_items: Was `project_state/decision_packet.md` treated as the only task authority?
Was `project_state/task_packet.json` treated as background only?
Did `decision_meta` remain valid, `APPROVED`, and aligned with active `reverse-agent-iteration@v2`?
Was the previous governance context registry round treated as accepted-with-limitations baseline?
Did this round supersede the smaller unexecuted state-hygiene retention plan rather than execute both?
Were existing state manifest, context packet, workstream registry, and prior state hygiene inventory inspected before adding new code?
Did the implementation avoid duplicating existing command-plan, execution-log, report-summary, closeout, context-builder, manifest, and workstream mechanisms?
Was `project_state/retention_policy.json` generated?

Does `retention_policy.json` classify current audit evidence, accepted-round evidence, generated gate artifacts, historical nonblocking artifacts, transient closeout logs/pids, missing sample references, docs/config, unknown files, and future disposable candidates?
Does retention policy explicitly forbid deletion without a future cleanup-apply decision?
Was `project_state/gates/cleanup_plan.json` generated?
Does cleanup plan only produce retain/archive-candidate/delete-candidate recommendations and no destructive actions?
Does every destructive recommendation include `delete_allowed_now=false`, `requires_future_cleanup_apply_decision=true`, and `requires_tombstone_if_deleted=true`?
Does cleanup plan classify `run_closeout_*.out.log`, `run_closeout_*.err.log`, and `run_closeout_*.pid` as transient candidates without deleting them?
Does cleanup plan classify missing historical sample artifacts as nonblocking references rather than current evidence gaps?
Does cleanup plan preserve current decision, report, pytest, command-plan, execution-log, final-check, closeout, state manifest, context packet, workstreams, and accepted-round minimum evidence?
Was `project_state/gates/archive_index.json` generated?
Does archive index use only bounded archive sources and avoid recursive full-rounds scanning?
Does archive index separate current, archived, historical_nonblocking, and candidate-for-future-archive entries?
Was `project_state/gates/deletion_manifest_schema.json` generated as schema-only evidence?
Was `project_state/gates/tombstone_schema.json` generated as schema-only evidence?
Did the round avoid writing any real deletion manifest or real tombstone?
Was `project_state/state_lifecycle_registry.json` generated?
Does lifecycle registry connect retention classes, cleanup-plan actions, archive-index roles, deletion schema, tombstone schema, and future cleanup-apply preconditions?
Was `project_state/gates/state_governance_bundle_result.json` generated?
Was `project_state/gates/state_governance_bundle_snapshot.json` generated?
Do new gate artifacts carry current decision/report/round IDs?

Does the governance bundle gate prove no deletion, move, archive compaction, tombstone write, database, runner dispatch, model API, external tool, CI dispatch, Web runtime, or real sample processing occurred?
Were `project_state/state_manifest.json`, `project_state/context/current_context_packet.json`, and `project_state/roadmap/workstreams.json` updated for this round?
Does `workstreams.json` mark only `state_governance_bundle_big_step` as `ACTIVE_ROUND`?
Does `workstreams.json` mark `project_governance_context_registry` as accepted baseline?
Does `workstreams.json` keep cleanup-apply, runner dispatch, database indexing, IDA/Ghidra/debugger integration, dynamic reverse solving, Web runtime, and CI mutation deferred or non-active?
Did command-plan authorize every executed command?
Were command-plan omitted commands left unexecuted?
Did pytest_result record real commands and exit codes?
Did focused tests cover retention policy, cleanup plan, archive index, deletion/tombstone schemas, lifecycle registry, governance bundle gate, and no-delete behavior?
Did existing project governance/gate/report tests continue to pass?
Did final-check pass or pass-with-limitations only for explicitly nonblocking historical sample artifact gaps?
Did report-summary synthesis pass and match the report summary?
Did run-closeout pass if authorized?
Were forbidden files untouched?
Were `.github/workflows/*`, `.codex-skills/*`, `solve_reports/*`, `project_state/archives/*`, and `project_state/deletions/*` untouched?
Did the final report avoid any solved/static/runtime/audit verification claim for concrete samples?
Did the final report explicitly state this round is planning/index/schema only and not cleanup-apply?
Did the final report recommend a future cleanup-apply round only after a separate decision accepts deletion manifest/tombstone design and deletion safety gates?
